info.title: Dev Health Agent Context Runtime API
info.description: Private hosted API for evidence-backed agent context packets, authorized provenance expansion, replay snapshots, and opt-in episode writeback. External Push is a separate API plane.

200.description: Liveness status
Service dependencies are ready

503.description: One or more service dependencies are not ready

200.description: Service, schema, entitlement, tool, and limit handshake
Generated context packet; status may be complete, partial, degraded, or empty
Persisted immutable packet snapshot

parameters.name: result_id
parameters.description: Scopes an acr:v1 evidence reference to the stored investigation result of the answer being verified. Without it the newest citing result answers (deprecated, logged).

200.description: Expanded evidence after independent organization and repository authorization
Existing episode returned for an identical idempotent retry

204.description: Episode accepted with no retained representation

200.description: Investigation result; status may be complete, partial, degraded, clarification_required, or no_match. schema_version is context_fabric_investigation_result.v1, or .v2 when the result minted an anchor membership-verify offer (CHAOS-4042). The body is the result plus, when the request asked synthesis_mode client and the turn reached synthesis, synthesis_input: the input for the caller's model to write the answer from. The result read by id never carries it. When options.max_serialized_bytes is below the size of the result, the body is instead the bounded consumer projection (context_fabric_answer_projection.v1) sized to that option, with projection_budget.full_result_omitted true and result_id naming the stored result, which GET by id serves whole against the service ceiling. A synthesis_mode client turn is never projected: its synthesis_input is outside options.max_serialized_bytes (the option bounds the result; the input has its own bound, the service ceiling), and a result over the option on such a turn is refused. text/event-stream (CHAOS-11909): served when Accept is exactly text/event-stream and the deployment has ACR_CONTEXT_FABRIC_EVENT_STREAM_ENABLED on; with the flag off the request gets 406 stream_unavailable before any admission work, and there is no fallback to application/json. Any other Accept value gets the application/json body, unchanged. The stream body is a sequence of Server-Sent Events frames -- `id: <seq>`, `event: <type>`, `data: <one event as one line of compact JSON, no field present as empty, zero or null>`, then a blank line -- and each data object validates against context_fabric_investigation_event.v1. accepted comes first, with the response headers, right after admission; stage events follow in the fixed stage order; a heartbeat follows when 10 seconds pass with no other event, so consecutive elapsed_ms values (accepted counting as 0) are at most 11 seconds apart (the bound is on silence; a heartbeat sooner than that is valid); exactly one terminal event, result or error, ends the stream. result.result is the application/json body this response has for the same request, byte for byte; error.error is the error.v1 envelope the same failure gets as an application/json error response, http_status included. A failure before the stream starts keeps its HTTP status and application/json error.v1 body. A stream that ends without a terminal event was interrupted. Run lease (CHAOS-11949): with ACR_CONTEXT_FABRIC_RUN_LEASE_ENABLED on, a stream request that names X-ACR-Submission-ID runs under a lease ACR holds instead of its connection: a disconnect does not cancel the run, every event goes to the run's event log first, GET /api/v1/context-fabric/investigations/submissions/{submission_id}/events attaches to it again (Last-Event-ID) from any replica, and POST .../cancel cancels it (terminal error canceled); a run whose replica stops ends error run_lost.

get.summary: Re-read one immutable investigation result by its opaque result_id.
get.description: Returns the canonical result a prior investigation persisted. A bounded consumer that received an answer projection uses this to fetch the full detail behind a claim, so every answer does not have to be inflated for the rare caller that wants everything; replay and diagnostics read the same way. Strictly read-only: no graph, canonical fact, or model work happens. view=projection returns the bounded answer projection instead of the canonical snapshot, produced by the same projection code the MCP answer tool calls, so a consumer cannot receive a different judgment from either surface. result_id is a frozen, opaque handle and must not be parsed. An unknown result_id, a malformed one, and one belonging to another organization are indistinguishable: all three answer 404, so result_id can never act as a cross-tenant existence oracle.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description: Representation to return. 'canonical' (default) returns the full context_fabric_investigation_result.v1 or .v2 (CHAOS-4042). 'projection' returns the bounded context_fabric_answer_projection.v1, produced by the SAME projection code the MCP answer tool uses, so the two surfaces cannot disagree about what an answer says.

parameters.name: max_drivers
parameters.description: Maximum drivers to retain in the projection view. Valid only with view=projection; omitted means the projection default. Every drop it causes is declared in projection_budget.

parameters.name: max_cohort_members
parameters.description: Maximum cohort members to retain in the projection view. Valid only with view=projection; omitted means the projection default. Every drop it causes is declared in projection_budget.

parameters.name: max_evidence_refs
parameters.description: Maximum evidence references the projection's index may carry. Valid only with view=projection; omitted means the projection default. Every drop it causes is declared in projection_budget.

200.description: Persisted immutable investigation result. The canonical snapshot by default (schema_version context_fabric_investigation_result.v1, or .v2 when the result minted an anchor membership-verify offer -- see CHAOS-4042), or its bounded consumer projection when view=projection.

get.summary: Read the caller's own submission record.
get.description: CHAOS-11913: the record of one X-ACR-Submission-ID the caller admitted on POST /api/v1/context-fabric/investigations. A client that lost a create response polls this (every 3 s) and replays result_id through GET /api/v1/context-fabric/investigations/{result_id} once the state is done; done_unsaved and abandoned mean ask again with a new submission id. Strictly read-only: it runs nothing. The read applies the record's reconcile rule: a running record whose reserved result is stored reads as done, and one past its budget plus 30 seconds reads as abandoned. The record is keyed by the authenticated principal: another principal's submission id, an unknown one and a malformed one all answer the same 404 not_found, so a submission id is never an existence oracle. Each read is authorized afresh.

200.description: The caller's submission record.

get.summary: Attach to the event stream of the caller's own leased run.
get.description: CHAOS-11949 (Ask Dev plan §2.7.9). With the deployment's run lease on (ACR_CONTEXT_FABRIC_RUN_LEASE_ENABLED), a create request that asks for the event stream and names X-ACR-Submission-ID runs under a lease ACR holds: a disconnect does not cancel it, and every event of its stream goes to a Postgres event log before it goes to the connection. This route attaches to that stream from any replica. Accept must be exactly text/event-stream. Without Last-Event-ID the stream replays from accepted; with it, from the event after that seq. The events are the run's own, byte for byte: the same seq, request_id and data as the stream the create request opened (so a client checks the events it saw first followed by the attach's events as one stream). New events follow as the run writes them; while nothing is written for 10 seconds the response carries an SSE comment line ': keepalive' (no event, no seq). The stream ends with the run's terminal event: result carries the stored result exactly as GET /api/v1/context-fabric/investigations/{result_id} serves it to the caller now (the stored-result gate decides it again, surface submission_attach); error carries the run's error.v1 envelope -- the run's own failure, canceled (an explicit cancel), run_lost (its replica stopped and its lease of 15 seconds ended), or submission_unsaved (an answer that was served but not stored). The event log is bounded: it keeps the latest 128 non-terminal events of a run (ContextFabricInvestigationRunEventLogMaxEvents) and its terminal; it holds no result content and goes with its submission record (retention, thread delete, organization purge). A Last-Event-ID the log cannot serve -- malformed, repeated, never written, older than the kept window (no Last-Event-ID too, once accepted is gone), or at or past the terminal -- and a submission whose run was not leased are 410 cursor_expired (details.reason expired, ahead, ended, malformed or not_logged), before any stream: read the submission status and replay the result by id instead. The submission is keyed by the authenticated principal: another principal's id, an unknown, a malformed id and a turn of a deleted or expired thread answer the same 404 not_found. With the run lease off the route answers 404. Each attach is authorized afresh.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: The seq of the last event the client received: a decimal integer from 0 to 9007199254740991, no sign, no leading zero. Absent is 0: replay from accepted.

200.description: The run's event stream after the cursor, then its terminal.

410.description: cursor_expired: the event log cannot serve this cursor, or the run was not leased.

post.summary: Cancel the caller's own leased run.
post.description: CHAOS-11949 (Ask Dev plan §2.7.9). Cancels the run of the caller's submission when it runs under the deployment's run lease. 202: the run is running; the first request records the cancel time t_req (a repeat keeps it), and the replica holding the run cancels it -- at once on its own replica, within a second on another -- so it ends within 5 seconds (ContextFabricRunCancelEffectiveSeconds) with the terminal error canceled, and no model attempt starts after that. An answer that had already finished is kept: the run then ends with its result. 204: the submission is already final; nothing to cancel. 409 submission_in_progress (details.reason not_leased, Retry-After): the submission is running but was admitted without a lease, so nothing can stop it but its own end. The submission is keyed by the authenticated principal: another principal's id, an unknown, a malformed id and a turn of a deleted or expired thread answer the same 404 not_found, and change nothing. With the run lease off the route answers 404. No body.

202.description: The cancel is recorded; the run ends with error canceled unless its answer had already finished.

get.summary: Read the caller's feedback on one of its own Ask Dev results.
get.description: Whether the caller found the result correct and useful: yes, no or unset each, and when it was last set (absent when never set). A result GET /api/v1/context-fabric/investigations/{result_id} would not serve to the caller now (an unknown, malformed, another principal's or another organization's id, a result the caller's current grant does not admit, a withheld result, a result only a deleted or expired conversation names), and a result that completed no Ask Dev submission (it has no owner), get the read by id's own 404 not_found. Each call decides the read afresh; a decision that cannot be taken is 503. Strictly read-only.

200.description: The caller's feedback on the result.

post.summary: Set the caller's feedback on one of its own Ask Dev results.
post.description: Sets both flags (correct, useful: yes, no or unset) and answers what is stored. The body is the whole feedback, so a repeat is harmless; unset clears a flag. There is no free text. A malformed body is 400 invalid_request before anything about the result is decided. A result GET /api/v1/context-fabric/investigations/{result_id} would not serve to the caller now (an unknown, malformed, another principal's or another organization's id, a result the caller's current grant does not admit, a withheld result, a result only a deleted or expired conversation names), and a result that completed no Ask Dev submission (it has no owner), get the read by id's own 404 not_found. Each call decides the read afresh; a decision that cannot be taken is 503. The feedback is part of the result's backing set: it goes with the result's retention and an organization purge.

200.description: The feedback as stored.

get.summary: List the caller's own Ask Dev conversations.
get.description: One page of the authenticated principal's Ask Dev conversations (threads), newest last turn first, then thread_id. A thread is the submissions the principal admitted on POST /api/v1/context-fabric/investigations with one X-ACR-Thread-ID; it carries no answer content. Deleted and expired threads are not listed. Pass next_cursor back as cursor for the next page. Strictly read-only. Each read is authorized afresh.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Threads per page, 1 to 50; 20 when absent. Any other value is 400 invalid_request.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The next_cursor of the previous page. Opaque; a malformed or foreign value is 400 invalid_request.

200.description: One page of the caller's threads.

get.summary: Read the caller's own Ask Dev conversation.
get.description: The authenticated principal's thread: its retention, its expiry, and a page of at most 100 turns, oldest first, each with its submission state and the question it was admitted with. Without before, the page is the latest turns; earlier_turns_cursor, when present, reads the page before it. A done turn names its result_id when GET /api/v1/context-fabric/investigations/{result_id} would serve the result to the caller now (the stored-result gate admits the caller and the read's serving rules serve it), and carries result_withheld instead when it would not; that read decides again. A running turn is found again here after a reload. The thread is keyed by the principal: another principal's thread, an unknown, deleted, expired or malformed id all answer the same 404 not_found. Strictly read-only: it runs nothing. Each read is authorized afresh; a decision that cannot be taken is 503, never a partial thread.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: The earlier_turns_cursor of a previous read of this thread: serve the turns before it. Opaque; a malformed or foreign value is 400 invalid_request.

200.description: The caller's thread.

delete.summary: Delete the caller's own Ask Dev conversation.
delete.description: Deletes the authenticated principal's thread: from this response on, the thread and the results of its turns are not served on any read (thread, list, result by id, submission replay and status), and the retention job removes their rows. Idempotent and existence-neutral: a well-formed id answers 204 whether or not the caller has such a thread, and another principal's thread is never touched. A malformed id is 404 not_found. A turn that names a deleted thread is refused with 409 thread_closed.

204.description: No such thread of the caller remains.

200.description: Device authorization created

post.description: Dispatches by Content-Type (CHAOS-4013): application/json is the pre-existing RFC 8628 device-code grant, unchanged; application/x-www-form-urlencoded is the RFC 8693 workload token-exchange grant.

subject_token.description: The k8s projected ServiceAccount JWT, validated via Kubernetes TokenReview.

scope.description: Space-delimited requested scope; may only narrow the resolved binding's grant, never widen it.

200.description: Device grant redeemed once, or a workload token successfully exchanged

400.description: Pinned RFC device grant error, or an RFC 8693 token-exchange error

200.description: Bounded device grant approved or advisory hints previewed
Current credential rotated with rollback receipt
Current credential revoked
Current credential acknowledged

get.summary: Direct data catalogue (data_catalog), CHAOS-7072 S1a: the operations, subject kinds, relationship types, limits and versions for THIS caller. The sections query parameter (comma list of operations, facts, subjects, relationships, limits) filters; the facts section lists the kinds read_facts serves, or says it is not available. A caller without data:read sees the operation list with available=false.

parameters.name: sections
parameters.description: Comma list of sections; empty = all. An unknown section is 400 invalid_request.

200.description: The catalogue for the caller.

post.summary: Direct subject lookup (find_subjects), CHAOS-7072 S1a: mode list (kind) or name (query, kinds). Every subject returned passed the direct-read subject gate for the caller in the same call; total_known counts admitted subjects only. 503 when no graph is composed.

200.description: Admitted subjects, one page.

post.summary: Direct fact read (read_facts, CHAOS-7073). Returns registry facts for canonical subjects the caller may read, one coverage row per (kind, subject). No model runs. An unreadable subject and a missing one give the same answer. Malformed or out-of-bounds requests answer 400 invalid_request; a missing or failed fact reader answers a retryable 503 upstream_unavailable.

200.description: The acr-data.v1 read_facts document. status is complete, partial, denied or unavailable; read coverage before relying on facts.

post.summary: Direct relationship read (read_relationships, CHAOS-7074). Returns the edges of one canonical subject the caller may read, depth 1 or 2, one keyset page at a time (page.next_cursor). Every end node passes the subject gate and every edge passes the edge gate (its own authorization attributes and both end nodes); a withheld edge is only counted (withheld.edges_not_visible). An edge shows a relation, not a cause. No model runs. A root the caller may not read and a missing one give the same answer (status denied, denied_or_not_found). Malformed requests and refused cursors answer 400 invalid_request; a missing or failed reader answers a retryable 503 upstream_unavailable.

200.description: The acr-data.v1 read_relationships page. status is complete, partial or denied; follow page.next_cursor until page.complete.

post.summary: Registered analytics operation (run_operation), CHAOS-7072 S1a. Requires the data:read scope. A typed result is HTTP 200: call is served, refused (with refusal.code), operation_unavailable, upstream_error or upstream_timeout. 501 feature_not_enabled with details.reason data_query_not_configured when the internal query service is not configured; 503 when the subject gate is unavailable.

200.description: Terminal typed result.

post.summary: Validated free-form GraphQL query (graphql_query), CHAOS-7075 S1b. Requires the data:read scope. acr validates the query against the allowed schema (data_catalog section schema) and sends only its own rebuilt text to the MCP listener. A typed result is HTTP 200: call is served, refused (with refusal.code), operation_unavailable, upstream_error or upstream_timeout. 501 feature_not_enabled with details.reason data_graphql_not_configured when the MCP listener is not configured; 503 when the subject gate is unavailable.

200.description: Terminal typed result.

max_window_days.description: The widest range or trailing window, in days, one read_facts call takes for this kind. A read over several kinds is held to the smallest.

schema.description: graphql_query: the allowed part of the ops schema for this credential (CHAOS-7075).

kind.description: List mode: exactly one subject kind.

query.description: Name mode: exact label, alias or provider key (at most 256 characters).

cursor.description: Opaque keyset position from page.next_cursor. It carries no permission.

owned_by.description: owned_by mode: a team canonical_id; returns the repositories and projects the team owns (CHAOS-7126).

handle.description: handle mode: one pull request number, work item key or CI run id (CHAOS-7126). Matches the caller may not read are neither returned nor counted.

anchor.description: handle mode only: a repository (for a pull request number or CI run id) or a project (for a work item key) that narrows the handle to one subject. Any other pairing is refused. kind and id come together. The anchor is checked for your credential like any subject; one you may not read, or that does not exist, gives the same empty answer as an anchor with no match.
Echo of the handle-mode anchor. The id is untrusted text.

operation.description: A served operation name from data_catalog.

variables.description: Allowlisted variable paths only; orgId is never a client variable.

max_bytes.description: Budget for the serialized data; 0 = 32768, values above 262144 are clamped.

data.description: The fixed shape of the registered document, after the output allowlist. Untrusted content.

status.description: The query service's HTTP status. Present with class http_status.

graphql_code.description: The GraphQL error code the query service returned, as a closed token; other for any code not listed.

variable.description: The GraphQL variable the query service named in its rejection.

message.description: The upstream GraphQL error message, bounded; untrusted upstream text. Present with class graphql_errors.

path.description: The upstream GraphQL error path, dot-joined; untrusted upstream text. Present with class graphql_errors.

query.description: One GraphQL query operation over the allowed schema. No mutation, subscription, fragment, directive or introspection; aliases on root fields only; orgId is never a client argument.

variables.description: Values for the variables the query declares.

max_bytes.description: Budget for the serialized data; 0 = 32768, values above 262144 are clamped.

data.description: Keyed by the client's root response keys; only the selected allowed fields. Untrusted content.

status.description: The data service's HTTP status. Present with class http_status.

graphql_code.description: The GraphQL error code the data service returned, as a closed token; other for any code not listed. graphql_validation_failed and graphql_parse_failed with HTTP 422 mean the request variables or document were rejected (call refused, code invalid_request).

variable.description: The GraphQL variable the data service named in its rejection.

message.description: The upstream GraphQL error message, bounded; untrusted upstream text. Present with class graphql_errors.

path.description: The upstream GraphQL error path, dot-joined; untrusted upstream text. Present with class graphql_errors.

webAssertionAuth.name: X-ACR-Web-Assertion
webAssertionAuth.description: Ed25519 request-bound compact JWT assertion for read-only server-to-server web requests. Assertions require the configured issuer, audience, local JWKS key ID, exact method/path/body hash, explicit repository scopes, and a maximum 30-second lifetime.

RequestID.name: X-Request-ID
RequestID.description: Optional correlation ID for request tracing and audit. The service generates and returns a request ID when absent or invalid. It does not authenticate or authorize the caller.

WaitBudget.name: X-ACR-Wait-Budget-Seconds
WaitBudget.description: Optional longest wait, in whole seconds, the caller will give one investigation. At least 10. The request ends by then, narrowing the service's own request timeout and never extending it: when the synthesis model call has not finished, the answer is served degraded with its result_id and coverage.details[code=synthesis_model_failed]. Stages before synthesis that run past the budget still end as 504 deadline_exceeded. A value that is not a whole number of seconds of at least 10 is ignored. For a user-class credential the per-call access read (CHAOS-12092) runs inside this budget: when what is left after it is below 10 seconds, the request is 503 budget_exhausted (retryable), refused before admission with nothing run.

ClientVersion.name: X-ACR-Client-Version
ClientVersion.description: Required SemVer compatibility signal for protected routes. It is advisory only and does not authenticate or authorize the caller; unsupported versions return 426 version_mismatch.

SubmissionID.name: X-ACR-Submission-ID
SubmissionID.description: Optional id of one user submit (CHAOS-11912): 8 to 128 characters of letters, digits, '.', '_', ':' and '-' (a UUID fits). The service admits the id once for the authenticated principal, bound to the request's semantic digest (every body field but request_id and consumer.name/consumer.version; consumer.surface is included, trimmed), and runs the request at most once under it. A repeat of an admitted id never runs the request again: a done submission is answered with its stored result exactly as GET /api/v1/context-fabric/investigations/{result_id} serves it, re-authorized for the caller; any other repeat is a 409 submission_mismatch, submission_in_progress (with Retry-After), submission_unsaved or submission_abandoned. A result that completes a submission is served to that submission's principal only, on every read surface. A malformed value is 400 invalid_request. A browser-class credential (CHAOS-12093) must name exactly one well-formed id on every create: a missing, malformed or repeated header is 400 submission_required, refused before admission and model work. Absent, for any other credential, the request runs at most once and is not repeatable, and its result keeps organization-bearer reads; when it runs on the deployment's model it is admitted under a server-minted key against the same shared limits (429 concurrency_limited / allowance_exhausted).

ThreadID.name: X-ACR-Thread-ID
ThreadID.description: Optional id of the conversation this turn belongs to (CHAOS-11913): the same grammar as X-ACR-Submission-ID. A conversation turn is a submission: X-ACR-Thread-ID without X-ACR-Submission-ID is 400 invalid_request (CHAOS-11948). The service stores it on the submission record, the status read returns it, and the turn (with its question) joins the caller's conversation of that id. It is not part of the request digest: a retry of a submission id keeps the first admission's thread. A malformed value is 400 invalid_request. The id names an Ask Dev conversation of the authenticated principal: the conversation is the caller's submissions under this id, keyed by organization, principal and id, so another principal's turn with the same id is never part of it. A turn whose id names a conversation of the caller that was deleted or has expired is refused with 409 thread_closed and nothing runs, as long as the service holds the conversation's closure record (at least until its expires_at); a client mints a new id per conversation.

ThreadRetentionDays.name: X-ACR-Thread-Retention-Days
ThreadRetentionDays.description: Optional retention of the Ask Dev conversation this turn belongs to (with X-ACR-Thread-ID): exactly 0 (kept until 24 hours after the conversation's last turn) or 30 (kept until 30 days after it). The latest turn of a conversation that names a value decides; a conversation whose turns named none has 0. When the retention ends, the conversation and the results of its turns are no longer served on any read and are deleted. It is not part of the request digest: a retry of a submission id keeps the first admission's value. Any other value, a repeated header, or the header without X-ACR-Thread-ID is 400 invalid_request.

Error.description: Structured safe error. On every protected route, a call by a user-class credential (browser, OAuth user, native device) re-reads the user's access live (CHAOS-12092): 403 access_denied when the user is not a member, is impersonating, the browser credential's session is not live, or the organization or user is unknown (one code for every reason); 403 feature_not_enabled when a required flag is off (agent_context_runtime, and ask_dev for the browser class), except on capabilities, which reports the live flag (200, entitlement false); 409 no_repository when the credential's grant within the organization's live repository inventory is empty; 503 upstream_unavailable when the read fails.

ContextFabricInvestigationBadRequest.description: Structured safe error. When the request carries supplied_synthesis without a supplied_interpretation, code is invalid_request and details.reason is supplied_interpretation_required.

ContextFabricInvestigationConflict.description: Structured safe error. A supplied interpretation or supplied synthesis that was made under a contract this service does not run carries details.interpretation_contract or details.synthesis_contract. A supplied synthesis written from an input that is no longer the turn's input carries details.reason input_changed and details.synthesis_input, the new synthesis input. A repeat of an admitted X-ACR-Submission-ID (CHAOS-11912) is a 409 with code submission_mismatch (a different request used the id; not retryable), submission_in_progress (its run is still live; retryable, with Retry-After), submission_unsaved (answered, not stored; not retryable) or submission_abandoned (ended without an answer, or ran past its budget plus 30 seconds; not retryable). None of them runs the request. A turn whose X-ACR-Thread-ID, or X-ACR-Submission-ID, belongs to a conversation of the caller that was deleted, has expired or is full (1000000 turns) is a 409 with code thread_closed (not retryable; start a new conversation). It runs nothing. A create by a browser-class credential that names no single well-formed X-ACR-Submission-ID is a 400 with code submission_required (not retryable as sent; CHAOS-12093). It runs nothing.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying the same submission id. Sent with submission_in_progress only.

synthesis_contract.description: The synthesis contract refusal: each contract field that is absent or differs, and the contract the service runs.

ContextFabricInvestigationForbidden.description: Structured safe error. feature_not_enabled with details.reason service_model_not_entitled: a caller asked for an investigation that runs on the service's own model (interpretation, synthesis, or both), and the organization has no model configuration of its own and does not hold both acr_service_model and the platform admin grant platform_model_fallback. feature_not_enabled with details.reason own_model_gate_closed: the organization's own model configuration is saved but behind a closed byo_llm plan gate (for example a lapsed plan); the service's model is never used in its place. feature_not_enabled with details.reason ai_features_turned_off: the organization has a saved model configuration but acr_service_model is OFF (its own override), so ACR AI features are turned off for it. feature_not_enabled with details.reason byo_no_investigate_config: the organization's saved BYO model keys are for other purposes only and none is set for investigations; it is a BYO organization, so the service's model is never used in its place, even with platform_model_fallback. feature_not_enabled with details.reason own_model_turned_off: an organization admin turned the saved model configuration off (kept, not deleted), so the organization has no usable own model, and it does not hold both acr_service_model and platform_model_fallback; the service's model is never used in its place. No model call was made and nothing was stored in either case. Only service_model_not_entitled is served on the caller's own model: the same question with a supplied interpretation and synthesis_mode client. The other reasons refuse that path too, because the service's phrasing step still binds a model. Credential and web assertion callers are decided on the same rule. access_denied (CHAOS-12092): a call by a user-class credential whose live access read refuses it (not a member, impersonating, a browser session that is not live, or an unknown organization or user); one code for every reason.

ContextFabricInvestigationStreamUnavaila.description: Structured safe error with code stream_unavailable (CHAOS-11909): the request asked for the event stream (Accept: text/event-stream) and the deployment has ACR_CONTEXT_FABRIC_EVENT_STREAM_ENABLED off. Written before any admission work: no investigation ran and nothing was stored. Not retryable; there is no fallback to application/json.

ContextFabricInvestigationUnprocessable.description: Structured safe error. A supplied synthesis the service rejected carries code synthesis_rejected and details.rejection_reason, a closed token.

ContextFabricInvestigationTooManyRequest.description: Structured safe error. rate_limited: the per-replica request rate limit (with N replicas the effective ceiling is N times the configured one). CHAOS-11914, for a request that names a NEW X-ACR-Submission-ID, and (CHAOS-11997) for a request without the header that runs on the deployment's model: concurrency_limited when the principal (details.limit principal) or the organization (details.limit org) already has its shared limit of running Ask Dev runs (defaults 2 and 4, counted across every replica); allowance_exhausted when the organization admitted its monthly allowance of runs on the deployment's model (default 1000, calendar month UTC; a run on the organization's own model counts to concurrency only). concurrency_limited and allowance_exhausted always carry Retry-After (for allowance_exhausted, the start of the next UTC month) and admitted and counted nothing. rate_limited carries Retry-After only when the request limiter knows the wait; a rate_limited answer from the model or graph runtime carries none, comes after admission, and its run stays counted (its submission record ends abandoned). A repeat of an already admitted submission id is never refused by these limits.
